title: SAT 07 · Place value and notation
description: A/B reasoning practice. Difficulty is editorial, not standardized SAT calibration.

questions.title: Reading a Place-Value Table
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table lists each digit and its place in a number. What number does it represent? Choose A or B and explain how each digit contributes to the total.
questions.explanation: The digits contribute \(30{,}000\), \(4{,}000\), \(0\), \(70\), and \(2\). Adding them gives \(30{,}000+4{,}000+70+2=34{,}072\). Choice B places the \(7\) in the hundreds place instead of the tens place, so it represents a different number.

visuals.alt: A place-value table lists 3 in the ten-thousands place, 4 in the thousands place, 0 in the hundreds place, 7 in the tens place, and 2 in the ones place.

questions.hint: Multiply each digit in the table by the value of its place, then add the results.

questions.title: Choosing the Correct Expanded Form
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which expanded form equals \(56{,}308\)? Choose A or B and justify the value of each nonzero digit.
questions.explanation: In \(56{,}308\), the digits represent \(5\) ten-thousands, \(6\) thousands, \(3\) hundreds, \(0\) tens, and \(8\) ones. Therefore, its expanded form is \(50{,}000+6{,}000+300+8=56{,}308\). Choice A adds \(80\), incorrectly putting the \(8\) in the tens place.
questions.hint: Name the place of each digit in 56,308, especially the 8, and write the value of each nonzero digit.

questions.title: The Value Contributed by a Digit
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The mapping shows how each digit in \(47{,}261\) contributes to the number. What is the value contributed by the digit \(7\)? Choose A or B and explain using its place.
questions.explanation: In \(47{,}261\), the digit \(7\) is in the thousands place, so its contribution is \(7\times1{,}000=7{,}000\). Choice A would be correct if the \(7\) were in the hundreds place, but it is not.

visuals.alt: The digits 4, 7, 2, 6, and 1 map respectively to contributions 40,000, 7,000, 200, 60, and 1.

questions.hint: Identify which place the 7 occupies in 47,261 and multiply 7 by that place value.

questions.title: Rounding to the Nearest Thousand
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Round \(48{,}627\) to the nearest thousand. Choose A or B and explain which digit determines whether the number rounds up or down.
questions.explanation: The thousands digit is \(8\), and the hundreds digit is \(6\). Because the hundreds digit is at least \(5\), increase the thousands digit by \(1\) and replace the digits to its right with zeros. The result is \(49{,}000\). Choice B would be used if the hundreds digit were less than \(5\).
questions.hint: Look at the digit just to the right of the thousands place to decide whether to round up or down.

questions.title: Writing a Number in Scientific Notation
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which standard-form number is equal to \(6.08\times10^5\)? Choose A or B and show how the decimal point moves.
questions.explanation: Since \(10^5=100{,}000\), \(6.08\times10^5=6.08\times100{,}000=608{,}000\). Equivalently, the decimal point moves five places to the right. Choice A corresponds to \(6.8\times10^5\), not \(6.08\times10^5\).
questions.hint: Multiply 6.08 by the power of ten by moving the decimal point five places to the right, filling with zeros.

questions.title: Expanded Form Across Place Values
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which expression is the expanded form of \(3{,}050{,}407\)? Choose A or B and account for the zero digits.
questions.explanation: The number has \(3\) millions, \(5\) ten-thousands, \(0\) thousands, \(4\) hundreds, \(0\) tens, and \(7\) ones. Thus the nonzero contributions sum to \(3{,}000{,}000+50{,}000+400+7=3{,}050{,}407\). Choice B uses \(5{,}000\), which places the digit \(5\) in the thousands place rather than the ten-thousands place.
questions.hint: List the place of every digit in 3,050,407, including the zeros, and write the value of each nonzero digit.

questions.title: Converting a Base-Five Numeral
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The chart gives the decimal value of each place in base five. What is the value of \(243_5\) in base ten? Choose A or B and show the weighted sum.
questions.explanation: In \(243_5\), the digits represent \(2\) groups of \(25\), \(4\) groups of \(5\), and \(3\) groups of \(1\). Therefore, \(243_5=2(25)+4(5)+3(1)=50+20+3=73\) in base ten. Choice B overcounts the total by \(10\).

visuals.alt: A bar chart shows that the base-five places 5 to the zero, 5 to the first, and 5 to the second have decimal place values 1, 5, and 25.

questions.hint: Use the chart's place values: multiply each base-five digit by the value of its place, then add.

questions.title: Rounding a Decimal to Hundredths
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Round \(3.846\) to the nearest hundredth. Choose A or B and explain how the thousandths digit affects the hundredths digit.
questions.explanation: The hundredths digit is \(4\), and the thousandths digit is \(6\). Since \(6\ge5\), increase the hundredths digit from \(4\) to \(5\) and remove the remaining digits. The rounded value is \(3.85\). Choice A would be correct if the thousandths digit were less than \(5\).
questions.hint: Find the hundredths digit and look at the digit immediately after it to decide whether it changes.

questions.title: Scientific Notation for a Small Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which expression is the scientific notation of \(0.000703\), with a coefficient at least \(1\) and less than \(10\)? Choose A or B and justify the exponent.
questions.explanation: Moving the decimal point in \(0.000703\) four places to the right gives \(7.03\), so the power of ten must be \(10^{-4}\) to preserve the value. Indeed, \(7.03\times10^{-4}=0.000703\). Choice B equals \(0.00703\), which is ten times as large.
questions.hint: Count how many places the decimal point must move to give a coefficient between 1 and 10; moving it right means a negative exponent.

questions.title: A Place Value Read from a Power Graph
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The graph shows the function \(y=10^x\). Use the value at \(x=3\) to find the contribution of the leading digit \(4\) in \(4.68\times10^3\). Choose A or B and explain the two steps.
questions.explanation: The graph shows that \(10^3=1{,}000\). The leading digit \(4\) therefore contributes \(4\times1{,}000=4{,}000\) to \(4.68\times10^3\). Choice A uses \(100\) as the place value, as if the exponent were \(2\) instead of \(3\).

visuals.alt: The graph of y equals 10 to the power x includes the point (3, 1000), showing that 10 cubed equals 1,000.

questions.hint: Read 10^3 from the graph, then multiply the leading digit by that place value.

questions.title: Rounding to Three Significant Figures
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Round \(0.004096\) to three significant figures. Choose A or B and explain why the final zero in the correct result is meaningful.
questions.explanation: The first three significant digits are \(4\), \(0\), and \(9\). The next digit is \(6\), so the \(9\) rounds up, producing \(0.00410\). The trailing zero records the precision of three significant figures. Choice B fails to round up when the next digit is \(6\).
questions.hint: Start counting significant digits at the first nonzero digit; use the next digit to round, and keep any zero the rounding produces.

questions.title: Converting a Binary Numeral
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: What is the base-ten value of the binary numeral \(101101_2\)? Choose A or B and expand it using powers of two.
questions.explanation: The binary digits correspond to \(32,16,8,4,2,1\). Thus \(101101_2=1(32)+0(16)+1(8)+1(4)+0(2)+1(1)=32+8+4+1=45\). Choice A is \(101011_2\), not the given digit sequence.
questions.hint: Write the place values of the six binary positions from right to left as powers of two, then add those where the digit is 1.

questions.title: Cards Classified by Their Digits
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A deck contains \(24\) different three-digit number cards. Set \(P\) contains cards whose hundreds digit is \(5\); set \(Q\) contains cards whose tens digit is \(0\). The Venn diagram gives the number of cards in each region. How many cards belong to neither set? Choose A or B and justify the count.
questions.explanation: The number in at least one set is \(6+5+4=15\), counting the intersection once. Equivalently, \(|P\cup Q|=10+9-4=15\). Therefore, \(24-15=9\) cards belong to neither set. Choice A equals \(24-(6+5)\), which fails to remove the \(4\) cards in the intersection and wrongly counts them as neither.

visuals.alt: Among 24 three-digit number cards, 6 have hundreds digit 5 only, 5 have tens digit 0 only, 4 satisfy both conditions, and 9 satisfy neither.

questions.hint: Add the three regions inside the circles, counting the overlap once, then compare with the total number of cards.

questions.title: Finding a Digit from a Rounded Number
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A four-digit number has the form \(63\Box8\), where \(\Box\) is one digit. The number rounds to \(6{,}400\) to the nearest hundred. Which digit can replace \(\Box\)? Choose A or B and justify the rounding.
questions.explanation: The hundreds digit is \(3\), and the tens digit determines rounding to the nearest hundred. To round up to \(6{,}400\), the tens digit must be at least \(5\). A \(7\) gives \(6{,}378\), which rounds to \(6{,}400\); a \(4\) gives \(6{,}348\), which rounds to \(6{,}300\). Therefore, choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Rounding to the nearest hundred depends on the tens digit; decide which tens digits make 63_8 round up.

questions.title: A Decimal Digit and Rounding
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The number is \(5.2a7\), where \(a\) is a digit. The table shows the result of rounding selected examples to the nearest tenth. If \(5.2a7\) rounds to \(5.3\), which statement about \(a\) must be true? Choose A or B and explain the threshold.
questions.explanation: When rounding \(5.2a7\) to the nearest tenth, the hundredths digit \(a\) determines whether \(5.2\) stays or rounds up. The result is \(5.3\) precisely when \(a\ge5\), so \(a\) can be \(5,6,7,8,\) or \(9\). Choice A lists digits that make the number round to \(5.2\), not \(5.3\).

visuals.alt: Examples show that 5.207 and 5.247 round to 5.2, while 5.257 and 5.297 round to 5.3, illustrating the change when the hundredths digit reaches 5.

questions.hint: When rounding to the nearest tenth only the hundredths digit decides; use the table to see where the result changes.

questions.title: An Exact Fraction for a Repeating Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which fraction is exactly equal to \(0.\overline{36}=0.363636\ldots\)? Choose A or B and derive the fraction rather than treating the decimal as terminating.
questions.explanation: Let \(x=0.363636\ldots\). Then \(100x=36.363636\ldots\). Subtracting gives \(99x=36\), so \(x=\frac{36}{99}=\frac{4}{11}\). Choice B equals \(0.36\), a terminating decimal, and is not equal to the repeating decimal \(0.\overline{36}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the repeating decimal by a power of ten that shifts one whole repeating block, then subtract to remove the repeating part.

questions.title: A Numeral in an Unknown Base
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The base-\(b\) numeral \(3a2_b\) has base-ten value \(122\), where \(b\) is an integer with \(6\le b\le10\) and \(a\) is a digit satisfying \(0\le a<b\). Which pair \((b,a)\) is possible? Choose A or B and use place values to verify it.
questions.explanation: The numeral has value \(3b^2+ab+2\). For \(b=6\), this becomes \(108+6a+2=110+6a\), which equals \(122\) when \(a=2\). If \(b\ge7\), then \(3b^2+ab+2\ge3(7^2)+2=149\), already greater than \(122\), so no larger base works. Choice A gives \(108+18+2=128\), not \(122\).
questions.hint: Write the numeral as 3b^2+ab+2 and try the smallest allowed base first; notice how fast 3b^2 grows.

questions.title: The Interval for a Rounded Number
questions.learningObjective: Apply place value and notation and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A positive real number \(N\) rounds to \(3.40\times10^5\) to three significant figures. Assume rounding is to the nearest thousand and ties are rounded up. Which interval contains exactly all possible values of \(N\)? Choose A or B and explain both endpoints.
questions.explanation: The value \(3.40\times10^5\) is \(340{,}000\), and three significant figures require rounding to the nearest \(1{,}000\). Values from \(339{,}500\) up to but not including \(340{,}500\) round to \(340{,}000\). The lower endpoint is included because \(339{,}500\) rounds up; the upper endpoint is excluded because \(340{,}500\) rounds to \(341{,}000\). Choice B is far too wide and does not describe rounding to the nearest thousand.
questions.hint: Three significant figures here means the nearest thousand; find the halfway points on either side of 340,000 and decide which one is included.
